newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek president invites Spanish royals for visit.
newsitem.headline: Greek president invites Spanish royals for visit.

text.p: President Costis Stephanopoulos has invited Spain's King Juan Carlos and his Greek-born wife Queen Sophia for an official visit to Greece, the government said on Friday.
If the Spanish royals accept, it would be the first official visit by Queen Sophia since her brother, former king Constantine, fled the country in 1967.
She returned once in 1981 for a five-hour private visit to bury her mother, the late Queen Frederika, amidst anti-royalist protests.
"There is an invitation by the Greek head of state to the head of state of Spain," Greek government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.

Greece abolished the monarchy in a 1974 referendum. Critics say Constantine paid for cooperating with the 1967-1974 dictatorship for months, during which he signed hundreds of decrees, before attempting a failed counter-coup and then fleeing in late 1967.
Sophia married Juan Carlos, then a prince, in 1962. The Spanish king has visited Greece unofficially for yachting races.
Constantine's first visit since attending his mother's funeral in 1981 was in the summer of 1993 and set of a storm of protests and minor clashes.
He was accompanied by his family and said the holiday was meant to show his children their homeland.

Although he says he will not demand the restoration of the monarchy, he is fighting a 1994 socialist government law depriving him and the rest of the former Greek royal family of their citizenship and property in Greece.

A special court is expected to decided next year whether three prime pieces of property should be returned to Constantine. One, the summer home of Mon Repos on the island of Corfu, is where Britain's Prince Philip was born.

The great bulk of the royal property was given to the state in exchange for paying accumulated property taxes. Greece had billed Queen Sophia about 30 million drachmas ($125,000) in taxes dating to the 1960s before the deal was made.
